claims.claim: DataTrove models processing as a list of reusable pipeline blocks and supports platform-agnostic execution through local, Slurm and Ray executors.
claims.notes: Executor availability and optional dependencies depend on the installed DataTrove version.

claims.claim: DataTrove Documents carry text, an identifier and metadata, while PipelineStep.run consumes and yields a document generator with rank and world_size arguments.
claims.notes: Reader, filter, stats and writer steps specialize the shared generator contract.

claims.claim: DataTrove distributes input files across logical tasks; its README warns that tasks greater than the number of files leave tasks without data.
claims.notes: A task processes a shard of files; DataTrove does not automatically split one large file into arbitrary subfiles.

claims.claim: DataTrove records completed task markers under logging_dir/completions and recommends keeping the total task count unchanged when resuming a failed run.
claims.locator: Executors; task completion and retry caution
claims.notes: Completion markers do not make arbitrary external side effects exactly-once; output writers still need safe commit behavior.

claims.claim: LocalPipelineExecutor exposes tasks and workers as separate controls: tasks define the logical task count, while workers define how many tasks run concurrently.
claims.notes: Effective throughput also depends on file-size skew, I/O, memory and processing time.

claims.claim: DataTrove BaseFilter keeps a document when filter returns true and drops it when filter returns false; an exclusion_writer can persist dropped documents.
claims.notes: The optional tuple return can also attach a reason for the dropped document.

claims.claim: DataTrove's MinHash example separates deduplication into signature generation, bucket matching, cluster construction and a final filtering pass.
claims.locator: stage1 MinhashDedupSignature; stage2 MinhashDedupBuckets; stage3 MinhashDedupCluster; stage4 MinhashDedupFilter
claims.notes: The final filter must use the same source data and compatible sharding as signature generation.

claims.claim: The current DataTrove pyproject metadata declares version 0.10.1 and requires Python 3.11 or newer.
claims.notes: Main-branch metadata can change; pin a release and dependency lock for reproducible production runs.

claims.claim: The current DataTrove README documents inference-based synthetic generation with rollout functions, chunk checkpoints and a request cache for retry-safe generation.
claims.locator: Practical guides → Synthetic data generation; Recoverable generation
claims.notes: Inference extras and server/provider configuration are optional; generation quality still requires independent validation.
